_comment: Hand-decoded trigger assignments for the events the 3-bucket classifier cannot place. Keyed decodeTable[mapId][eventId]. convert.ts CONVERT_STRICT=1 fails the build on any dropped event missing a row, so this file must cover ALL of them -- but a row is only needed for an event NO decoded start reaches. trigger: 'OnExit' (gated map-exit cutscene; the bytecode HANDOFF performs the warp), 'Native' (compiled-MIPS handler -> host registry), or 'None' (acknowledged, emits no engine event). `if` is a compact AND-list of leaves [["flag", id, expected], ...]; ids may be hex strings. REMOVED 2026-10-05, all measured: every `None` row that named an event a decoded start already reaches (54 rows over 22 places). A `None` row emits NOTHING, so such a row could only mislead: the plan and the notes read as 'this scene is unreachable' when a ported system starts it. (1) 15 cutscene rows — s400/1300, s485/1530, s545/710, s585/460, s780/885, s795/830, s795/840, s795/1505, s800/850, s800/1506, s810/1035, s815/1040, s815/1041, s815/1050, s306/966 — were marked 'inert' by hand; 13 are the ported gate objects (engine/systems/scene-arrival.ts) or the ported op-8 step program (engine/systems/trigger-system.ts), and s795/1505 + s800/1506 are the places' SECOND per-place gate object, whose phase band is `phase1` (pro/wstag795.s:0x5b4-0x5d0, pro/wstag800.s:0x8c0-0x8dc: `beq phase,1 -> chain`). All 15 now have a converted row. (2) 24 native-handler rows — the fire-trap controllers (s741/9000-9015), the trap-pad switches (s745/8000-8002, s746/8000-8002), the Gunslinger layout switches (s810/9000-9001), the ambush-tile handlers (s550/9000, s551/9000) — already said 'unreachable: the step program owns this event'; their op-8 step rows are emitted by convertStoryStages from the step program. (3) 13 interactive-controller rows — the eight-topic help menus and the yes/no tutorials (s210/8,9,1510; s220/1512,1514,1516; s270/1518,1520; s280/1522; s924/1602,1604; s935/1616,1618) — are started by the bank-0x90 talk launcher (engine/systems/talk-launch.ts); their CONTROLLERS are ported as engine/dw3/ui/native/yesno-launcher.ts and help-menu-launcher.ts, and the controller routines themselves are the per-place gate objects tools/measure_gate_objects.py counts as `controllers`. Re-running convert.ts over the table without them changes web/assets/engine-content.json by exactly two rows: s795.auto.1505 and s800.auto.1506 appear, and the guessed s800.sb.post OnTalk row for 1506 goes away. KEPT: the OnExit gondola/exit rows (a trigger the disc does not have — see .bunny-scratch/prior/sceneengine-report.md 3.3 claim 16), and the two vestigial ambush rows s949/9000 + s953/9000, which no step program reaches and whose stage slot 5 is empty.

s305._comment: 660 and 661 no longer marked inert (2026-10-02): the hand mark was wrong. The stage-entry dispatcher starts BOTH — wstag305.s .L0x3b0 `bnez $v0,.L0x568` with `li $a0,0x294` (=660) in the delay slot, after the get_flag(0x1c36) call at .L0x394; .L0x3dc `bnez $v0,.L0x568` with `li $a0,0x295` (=661) after get_flag(0x1c37) at .L0x3c8; .L0x568 is the overlay's only `jal start_event` (0x800853f8). auto_event_gates.json already carried both gates. 661 is not inert in any case: its on_complete routine at file 0x6a8 is `lui $v1,0x8005 / li $v0,0x17 / jr $ra / sw $v0,-0x4c90($v1)` — it WRITES the master story ordinal 23, so it is that beat's closing scene, not a dropped cutscene. 965 and 1450 no longer marked inert either (2026-10-02): neither stores a story step - their event-table records at wstag305.s file 0x39ac / 0x39c0 carry on_complete_fn 0, i.e. no completion routine at all - and neither needs a row here, because neither is started by a row. 965 is started by the stage's POSITION step program: wstag305.s file 0x38b0, op 8 with params[0]=0x3c5, gated on get_flag(0x7094)==1 AND get_flag(0x7019)==0. Both are bank-0x70 progress-ordinal RANGE predicates (roster_predicate_table.json: 0x7094 = ordinal >= 30, 0x7019 = ordinal in [27,37]), so the record runs from story step 38 on. Its bytecode (file 0x21bc) walks the player to (392,245), says one line and ends `HANDOFF 537 88 524 5` (to s310); the grid cells that select the record are (11,7)(12,7)(13,7)(12,8)(13,8) = px x 352-447, y 224-287 (story_trigger_grids.json, cell 32). The OnStep row s305.step.evt965 that carries that start is emitted by convertStoryStages from the step program itself. 1450 is started by the bank-0x90 TALK launcher: set_flag(0x9061,1) = start_event(talk_event_launches.json events[97]) = start_event(1450), because fieldstg F0x8008bfa4 reads the u16 array at RAM 0x800978d8 and calls the same 0x800853f8 the op-8 step handler calls. Eight arena-champion dialogue states write 0x9061 in their on_close list in web/assets/scenes/s305.json - npc_id 63/198/199/289/290/291/292, every one of them the line estalk05#189 a champion says once you have beaten it, gated on the bank-0x1c champion-beaten tally (0x7070 = at least 2 of 0x1c27..0x1c33 still clear, 0x7071 = at least 1 set, 0x7073 = exactly 1 clear on the last one). Its bytecode (file 0x220c) is `WAIT 60 / HANDOFF 536 312 285 5`: it puts you back in the middle of the Master Room facing up. web/game.js playTalkEvent plays it (applyStoryFlag, bank 0x90), so a row here would start it twice. NOTE both records carry flag_key 012e000a - flag_key is NOT unique inside a stage, so playTalkEvent must resolve a launcher id by event id and only fall back to flag_key.

s741._comment: Fire Dungeon (second room). All 16 events share native_fn 0x28c -> the FIRE-TRAP controller F0x800a606c: a floor patch that takes field control, plays SWITCH02, and blows up each walking Digimon in turn, forcing its stored cur_hp to 1. Each event's on_complete sets its own gate flag (0x40ba..0x40c9), which its step record tests, so every patch is one-shot. Wired data-driven from web/assets/data/fire_traps.json (tools/extract_fire_traps.py) + engine/systems/fire-trap.ts, exactly as s745/s746's trap pads are wired from trapPads. These rows are now unreachable -- once the stage's event table resolves, every one of the 16 is an OnStep event and is skipped before the decode table -- and are kept only so the classification stays recorded. CORRECTION 2026-07-28: this entry previously described them as inert 'bug-maze controller spawn ... effect via scene warps'. That was wrong on both counts -- s741 is not a bug maze, and the controller is not ambient.

s220._comment: The Digimon Lab's events 53/54/55/56 and 1513/1515/1517 are the CHILDREN of the room's three Yes/No launchers (1512 -> 53/1513, 1514 -> 55/1515, 1516 -> 56/1517; engine/dw3/ui/native/yesno-launcher.ts, YESNO_LAUNCHERS). Six of them are now retired by lib.ts CONTROLLER_CHILDREN. Event 54 is the seventh and is different: nothing starts it. wstag220 has exactly three `jal 0x800853f8` (start_event) sites — .L0x490, .L0xa78, .L0x1060 — which load 0x35/0x5e9, 0x37/0x5eb, 0x38/0x5ed (53/1513, 55/1515, 56/1517); none loads 0x36 (54). The resident bank-0x90 table names 54 at bit 6 (0x9006), but no s220 NPC dialogue state writes 0x9006 (the stage's on_close ids are 36869/36871/36872 only), and no s220 scene or overlay code writes it. Authored content the disc never reaches.

54.note: No start site on the disc: wstag220's only three start_event calls load 53/1513, 55/1515, 56/1517 — never 54 — and no s220 NPC writes bank-0x90 bit 6 (0x9006) which the resident table would resolve to 54. The classifier's speaker-guessed s220.talk.54 row made the Digivolve Navi (npc 32) play a DIGIMON-NAVI scene (esdmg200[14]) instead of its own line, and swallowed the line — the operator's 'auto-advances into another NPC's conversation'.
